subject.title: fix(agents): keep bundle LSP tool names provider-safe

question: Should previously exposed unsafe or colliding bundled LSP tool identifiers intentionally migrate to the new provider-safe canonical names on upgrade?
rationale: The code fix is sound and valid complete names are preserved, but users on permissive providers or exact-name tool policies may have observed the formerly unsafe names; repository policy requires an explicit owner choice for that upgrade impact.

options.title: Accept Canonical Rename
options.body: Treat unsafe and colliding historical identifiers as non-contractual, land the safe names, and record the exact-name policy impact in merge or release context.

options.title: Preserve Policy Matching
options.body: Keep only provider-safe names model-facing but add a narrowly tested compatibility mechanism for legacy exact-name policy selectors if maintainers consider those shipped identifiers contractual.

options.title: Pause Pending Contract Evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until a shipped release or user report establishes whether unsafe generated identifiers were relied upon as a supported policy surface.

recommendation.title: Accept Canonical Rename
recommendation.body: Treat unsafe and colliding historical identifiers as non-contractual, land the safe names, and record the exact-name policy impact in merge or release context.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review routing explicitly surfaced this person for the remaining compatibility decision and the PR otherwise appears ready for normal owner review.
